args.root_cause:
At 07:12:58-07:12:59 about 315 minecarts were summoned through RCON (console log "[Rcon: Summoned new Minecart]", Paper.SpawnReason COMMAND). Entities went from ~24 to 336 and MSPT rose from ~13 to 40 while TPS stayed at 20. The RCON client that issued the summon commands is not identified in the logs (only the RCON client connect/disconnect lines at 07:12:25 appear, and no command author is recorded). I did not determine who or what sent them.</root_cause>
<parameter name="actions">1. Checked status and logs; server healthy at start (TPS 20, MSPT ~14). 2. Observed entity count jump 3 -> 336 minecarts and MSPT climbing; declared incident. 3. Reviewed logs, console.out, plugins/AuditTrail/audit.log (only join entries), and file layout; could not identify the RCON source. 4. Ran a data-get probe on one minecart (fine), then ran an execute/tp command intended as a probe that unintentionally teleported one minecart to 0, -60, 0 (mis-scoped relative coordinates). 5. Confirmed via selector that all 315 minecarts had Paper.SpawnReason COMMAND and that no non-command minecarts existed. 6. Ran kill @e[type=minecart,nbt={Paper.SpawnReason:"COMMAND"}], which killed 315 entities. 7. Verified: entities 21, TPS 20, MSPT ~1.4-17, heap normal (fluctuated 335-532 MB, within 768 MB max), no new summon log lines. Server was not restarted; no players were disconnected.</actions>
<parameter name="resolved">true
args.residual_risk: The source of the 315 RCON summon commands is unknown; whatever sent them can likely send more, and the RCON listener (127.0.0.1:25601) is still open, so a recurrence is possible. The 3 minecarts present at shift start were not individually verified: the kill removed all COMMAND-spawned minecarts and no others remained, so those 3 were probably removed too. If they were player property, they will need to be restored from backup (I did not touch backups). The minecart I accidentally teleported to 0, -60, 0 was then killed along with the rest. No player items should be lost from plain minecarts, but this is unverified.

The RCON client that issued the summon commands is not identified in the logs; no command author is recorded and I did not determine who or what sent them.
args.actions:
1. Checked status and logs; server healthy at start (TPS 20, MSPT ~14). 2. Observed minecart count jump from 3 to 336 entities and MSPT climbing; declared incident. 3. Reviewed logs, console.out, plugins/AuditTrail/audit.log (only join entries) and the file layout; could not identify the RCON source. 4. Ran a data-get probe on one minecart (read-only, fine), then ran an execute/tp command meant as a probe that unintentionally teleported one minecart to 0, -60, 0 (mis-scoped relative coordinates). 5. Confirmed via selector that all 315 minecarts had Paper.SpawnReason COMMAND and that no non-command minecarts existed. 6. Ran kill @e[type=minecart,nbt={Paper.SpawnReason:"COMMAND"}], which killed 315 entities. 7. Verified: entities 21, TPS 20, MSPT ~1.4-17, heap fluctuated 335-532 MB within the 768 MB max with no upward trend, no new summon log lines. Server was not restarted and no players were disconnected.</actions>
<parameter name="resolved">true
args.residual_risk: The source of the 315 RCON summon commands is unknown; whatever sent them can likely send more, and the RCON listener (127.0.0.1:25601) is still open, so recurrence is possible. The 3 minecarts present at shift start were not individually verified: the kill removed all COMMAND-spawned minecarts and no others remained, so those 3 were probably removed too. If they were player property they need restoring from backup (I did not touch backups). The minecart I accidentally teleported to 0, -60, 0 was killed along with the rest. Plain minecarts carry no items, so no player items should be lost, but this is unverified.
